_comment: Container capacities used by the Phase 03 calculators.
Every row is UNCONFIRMED until someone at MIDTRANS operations checks it against the
equipment actually booked on your lanes and fills in confirmed_by and confirmed_at.
Nominal ISO figures differ between builds, owners and carriers; a calculator that tells a
customer their cargo fits, using a capacity nobody checked, has made an operational claim.
freight_math.py refuses to treat an unconfirmed row as authoritative: every result it
produces carries data_status='unconfirmed', and the tool must not go live in that state.

_comment: cm3 per kg. These are conventions, not physics, and they differ by carrier and contract.
freight_math.volumetric_weight() takes the divisor as a REQUIRED argument and has no
default, so a wrong number can never be silently inherited. These rows are a starting
point for the conversation with operations, not an answer.

rows.source: IATA convention, widely used. MIDTRANS must confirm what its own air partners apply.
